sourceName: SIVORA NEET Physics Full Mock 1 Candidates
en_questionText: The dimensional formula of surface tension is:
en_explanation: Surface tension is force per unit length. Therefore its dimensions are [M L T⁻²]/[L] = [M T⁻²].

sourceName: SIVORA NEET Physics Full Mock 1 Candidates
en_questionText: The measured length and breadth of a rectangle are (5.0 ± 0.1) cm and (2.0 ± 0.1) cm. The maximum percentage error in its area is:
en_explanation: For A = lb, maximum fractional errors add: ΔA/A = 0.1/5.0 + 0.1/2.0 = 0.07, or 7%.

sourceName: SIVORA NEET Physics Full Mock 1 Candidates
en_questionText: A particle starts from rest with constant acceleration 4 m s⁻². Its displacement during the third second is:
en_explanation: Distance in the nth second is u + a(2n−1)/2. For u = 0, a = 4 m s⁻² and n = 3, the displacement is 10 m.

sourceName: SIVORA NEET Physics Full Mock 1 Candidates
en_questionText: A projectile is launched with speed 20 m s⁻¹ at 30° above the horizontal. Taking g = 10 m s⁻², its maximum height is:
en_explanation: The vertical component is 20 sin 30° = 10 m s⁻¹. Thus H = uᵧ²/(2g) = 100/20 = 5 m.

sourceName: SIVORA NEET Physics Full Mock 1 Candidates
en_questionText: A 5 kg block rests on a rough horizontal surface with coefficient of static friction 0.4. Taking g = 10 m s⁻², the minimum horizontal force that just starts its motion is:
en_explanation: The limiting static friction is μₛN = 0.4 × 5 × 10 = 20 N, so motion begins when the applied force reaches 20 N.

sourceName: SIVORA NEET Physics Full Mock 1 Candidates
en_questionText: When a person standing in a stationary bus falls backward as the bus starts suddenly, the effect is explained by:
en_optionD: Action and reaction acting on the same body
en_explanation: The feet move with the bus while the upper body tends to remain at rest due to inertia of rest, making the person fall backward relative to the bus.

sourceName: SIVORA NEET Physics Full Mock 1 Candidates
en_questionText: A net force increases the speed of a 2 kg body from 3 m s⁻¹ to 7 m s⁻¹. The net work done is:
en_explanation: By the work-energy theorem, W = ½m(v²−u²) = ½×2×(49−9) = 40 J.

sourceName: SIVORA NEET Physics Full Mock 1 Candidates
en_questionText: A body of mass m moving with speed v collides elastically head-on with a stationary body of mass 3m. The velocity of the first body immediately after collision is:
en_explanation: For a one-dimensional elastic collision, v₁ = (m−3m)v/(m+3m) = −v/2. The negative sign denotes reversal of direction.

sourceName: SIVORA NEET Physics Full Mock 1 Candidates
en_questionText: If the net external torque on a system is zero, which quantity remains constant?
en_explanation: The external torque equals the rate of change of angular momentum. Zero external torque therefore conserves angular momentum.

sourceName: SIVORA NEET Physics Full Mock 1 Candidates
en_questionText: A uniform disc of mass M and radius R rotates about an axis through its centre and perpendicular to its plane. Its radius of gyration is:
en_explanation: For the disc, I = MR²/2. Since I = Mk², k = R/√2.

sourceName: SIVORA NEET Physics Full Mock 1 Candidates
en_questionText: A wire of length L and cross-sectional area A extends by ΔL under force F. Its Young's modulus is:
en_explanation: Young's modulus is longitudinal stress divided by strain: (F/A)/(ΔL/L) = FL/(AΔL).

sourceName: SIVORA NEET Physics Full Mock 1 Candidates
en_questionText: Water flows steadily through a horizontal pipe. If its cross-sectional area becomes half, the flow speed becomes:
en_explanation: For incompressible steady flow, Av is constant. Halving the area therefore doubles the speed.

sourceName: SIVORA NEET Physics Full Mock 1 Candidates
en_questionText: A gas absorbs 300 J of heat and does 120 J of work. Its increase in internal energy is:
en_explanation: Using ΔU = Q − W for work done by the gas, ΔU = 300 − 120 = 180 J.

sourceName: SIVORA NEET Physics Full Mock 1 Candidates
en_questionText: A heat engine operating in a cycle cannot convert all absorbed heat into work because this would violate:
en_explanation: The Kelvin-Planck statement of the second law forbids a cyclic engine whose sole effect is complete conversion of heat from one reservoir into work.

sourceName: SIVORA NEET Physics Full Mock 1 Candidates
en_questionText: At the same temperature, the ratio of rms speeds of hydrogen and oxygen molecules, vH₂/vO₂, is:
en_explanation: vᵣₘₛ ∝ 1/√M. Hence vH₂/vO₂ = √(32/2) = 4.

sourceName: SIVORA NEET Physics Full Mock 1 Candidates
en_questionText: For an ideal monatomic gas in thermal equilibrium, the molar heat capacity at constant volume is:
en_explanation: A monatomic gas has three translational degrees of freedom, so Cᵥ = fR/2 = 3R/2.

sourceName: SIVORA NEET Physics Full Mock 1 Candidates
en_questionText: In simple harmonic motion of amplitude A, the kinetic energy equals the potential energy at displacement magnitude:
en_explanation: Total energy is kA²/2 and potential energy is kx²/2. Equality K = U makes U half the total, giving x² = A²/2 and |x| = A/√2.

sourceName: SIVORA NEET Physics Full Mock 1 Candidates
en_questionText: A string fixed at both ends has length 0.60 m. If wave speed is 120 m s⁻¹, its fundamental frequency is:
en_explanation: For a string fixed at both ends, f₁ = v/(2L) = 120/(1.20) = 100 Hz.

sourceName: SIVORA NEET Physics Full Mock 1 Candidates
en_questionText: The electric flux through a closed surface enclosing charge q is:
en_optionD: Dependent only on the surface area
en_explanation: Gauss's law gives the net flux through any closed surface as the enclosed charge divided by ε₀.

sourceName: SIVORA NEET Physics Full Mock 1 Candidates
en_questionText: Two capacitors of 3 μF and 6 μF are connected in series. Their equivalent capacitance is:
en_explanation: For series capacitors, C = C₁C₂/(C₁+C₂) = (3×6)/(3+6) = 2 μF.

sourceName: SIVORA NEET Physics Full Mock 1 Candidates
en_questionText: An electric dipole of moment p is placed in a uniform electric field E at 60° to the field. The work required to rotate it slowly to 120° is:
en_explanation: U = −pE cosθ. Thus ΔU = −pE cos120° + pE cos60° = pE/2 + pE/2 = pE.

sourceName: SIVORA NEET Physics Full Mock 1 Candidates
en_questionText: A 12 V battery is connected across a 4 Ω resistor. The current through the resistor is:
en_explanation: Ohm's law gives I = V/R = 12/4 = 3 A.

sourceName: SIVORA NEET Physics Full Mock 1 Candidates
en_questionText: A cell of emf 2.0 V and internal resistance 0.5 Ω supplies a current of 1.0 A. Its terminal potential difference is:
en_explanation: During discharge, terminal voltage is V = E − Ir = 2.0 − 1.0×0.5 = 1.5 V.

chapterName: Magnetic Effects of Current and Magnetism
sourceName: SIVORA NEET Physics Full Mock 1 Candidates
en_questionText: A charged particle moves parallel to a uniform magnetic field. The magnetic force on it is:
en_explanation: The magnetic force magnitude is qvB sinθ. For motion parallel to the field, θ = 0 and the force is zero.

chapterName: Magnetic Effects of Current and Magnetism
sourceName: SIVORA NEET Physics Full Mock 1 Candidates
en_questionText: The magnetic field at the centre of a circular coil of radius R carrying current I and having N turns is:
en_explanation: Each circular turn produces μ₀I/(2R) at the centre; for N turns the fields add to μ₀NI/(2R).

sourceName: SIVORA NEET Physics Full Mock 1 Candidates
en_questionText: According to Lenz's law, an induced current flows in a direction that:
en_optionA: Opposes the change in magnetic flux producing it
en_optionC: Is independent of the flux change
en_optionD: Always agrees with the applied current
en_explanation: Lenz's law states that the induced effect opposes the change in magnetic flux responsible for it, consistent with energy conservation.

sourceName: SIVORA NEET Physics Full Mock 1 Candidates
en_questionText: An alternating voltage has peak value 100√2 V. Its rms value is:
en_explanation: For a sinusoidal voltage, Vᵣₘₛ = V₀/√2 = 100√2/√2 = 100 V.

sourceName: SIVORA NEET Physics Full Mock 1 Candidates
en_questionText: Which electromagnetic radiation has a frequency higher than visible light but lower than X-rays?
en_explanation: In increasing frequency, the relevant order is visible, ultraviolet, X-rays. Infrared, microwaves and radio waves have lower frequencies than visible light.

sourceName: SIVORA NEET Physics Full Mock 1 Candidates
en_questionText: In a charging parallel-plate capacitor, the displacement current between the plates is:
en_optionA: Equal to the conduction current in the connecting wires
en_optionD: Present only after charging is complete
en_explanation: Continuity of current in Maxwell's theory requires the displacement current between the plates to equal the conduction current in the wires during charging.

sourceName: SIVORA NEET Physics Full Mock 1 Candidates
en_questionText: An object is placed 30 cm in front of a concave mirror of focal length 20 cm. The image distance from the mirror is:
en_optionA: 60 cm in front of the mirror
en_optionD: 12 cm in front of the mirror
en_explanation: Using 1/f = 1/v + 1/u with f = −20 cm and u = −30 cm gives 1/v = −1/20 + 1/30 = −1/60, so v = −60 cm: 60 cm in front.

sourceName: SIVORA NEET Physics Full Mock 1 Candidates
en_questionText: In Young's double-slit experiment, the slit separation is doubled while all other quantities remain unchanged. The fringe width becomes:
en_explanation: Fringe width β = λD/d. Doubling slit separation d reduces β to half.

sourceName: SIVORA NEET Physics Full Mock 1 Candidates
en_questionText: An astronomical telescope in normal adjustment has objective and eyepiece focal lengths 100 cm and 5 cm. Its angular magnification and tube length are, respectively:
en_explanation: For normal adjustment, magnification magnitude is fₒ/fₑ = 100/5 = 20 and tube length is fₒ + fₑ = 105 cm.

chapterName: Dual Nature of Matter and Radiation
sourceName: SIVORA NEET Physics Full Mock 1 Candidates
en_questionText: Light of photon energy 4.0 eV falls on a metal of work function 2.5 eV. The maximum kinetic energy of emitted photoelectrons is:
en_explanation: Einstein's photoelectric equation gives Kmax = hν − φ = 4.0 − 2.5 = 1.5 eV.

chapterName: Dual Nature of Matter and Radiation
sourceName: SIVORA NEET Physics Full Mock 1 Candidates
en_questionText: If the momentum of a particle is doubled, its de Broglie wavelength becomes:
en_explanation: The de Broglie relation is λ = h/p. Doubling momentum therefore halves the wavelength.

sourceName: SIVORA NEET Physics Full Mock 1 Candidates
en_questionText: In the Bohr model of hydrogen, the radius of the nth stationary orbit is proportional to:
en_explanation: For a hydrogen atom, rₙ = a₀n², so orbital radius is proportional to n².

sourceName: SIVORA NEET Physics Full Mock 1 Candidates
en_questionText: A radioactive sample has a half-life of 6 hours. The fraction remaining after 18 hours is:
en_explanation: Eighteen hours equals three half-lives, so the remaining fraction is (1/2)³ = 1/8.

sourceName: SIVORA NEET Physics Full Mock 1 Candidates
en_questionText: A p-n junction diode conducts strongly when it is:
en_optionA: Forward biased beyond its knee voltage
en_optionD: Connected with both terminals at the same potential
en_explanation: Forward bias lowers the junction barrier; appreciable conduction occurs after the applied voltage reaches the knee region.

sourceName: SIVORA NEET Physics Full Mock 1 Candidates
en_questionText: The output of a NAND gate is LOW only when its two inputs are:
en_explanation: A NAND gate is the negation of AND. AND is HIGH only for two HIGH inputs, so NAND is LOW only in that case.

sourceName: SIVORA NEET Physics Full Mock 1 Candidates
en_questionText: A screw gauge has pitch 1 mm and 100 divisions on its circular scale. Its least count is:
en_explanation: Least count equals pitch divided by circular-scale divisions: 1 mm/100 = 0.01 mm.

sourceName: SIVORA NEET Physics Full Mock 1 Candidates
en_questionText: In a metre-bridge experiment, an unknown resistance X in the left gap balances a 6 Ω resistance in the right gap at 40 cm from the left end. The value of X is:
en_explanation: At balance, X/6 = 40/(100−40) = 2/3. Therefore X = 6×2/3 = 4 Ω.

en_questionText: What mass of oxygen is required for the complete combustion of 4.0 g of methane according to CH₄ + 2O₂ → CO₂ + 2H₂O?
en_explanation: Four grams of CH₄ is 4/16 = 0.25 mol. It requires 0.50 mol O₂, whose mass is 0.50 × 32 = 16 g.

en_questionText: For a reaction at constant pressure, the system absorbs 50 kJ of heat and performs 20 kJ of expansion work. The change in internal energy is:
en_explanation: Using ΔU = q + w and taking work done by the system as w = −20 kJ, ΔU = 50 − 20 = +30 kJ.

en_questionText: A solution contains 0.50 mol of solute in 250 mL of solution. Its molarity is:
en_explanation: Molarity is moles per litre of solution: M = 0.50/0.250 = 2.0 mol L⁻¹.

en_questionText: At 25 °C, the pH of a 1.0 × 10⁻³ mol L⁻¹ aqueous HCl solution is closest to:
en_explanation: HCl is a strong acid, so [H⁺] ≈ 1.0 × 10⁻³ mol L⁻¹. Therefore pH = −log[H⁺] = 3.

en_questionText: According to VSEPR theory, the molecular shape of NH₃ is:
en_explanation: Nitrogen in NH₃ has three bond pairs and one lone pair. Its electron-pair geometry is tetrahedral and its molecular shape is trigonal pyramidal.

chapterName: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties
en_questionText: Which species has the smallest radius among O²⁻, F⁻, Na⁺ and Mg²⁺?
en_explanation: All four species are isoelectronic with 10 electrons. Radius decreases as nuclear charge increases, so Mg²⁺, with the greatest nuclear charge, is smallest.

en_questionText: The correct IUPAC name of [Co(NH₃)₅Cl]Cl₂ is:
en_explanation: The complex cation has charge +2; NH₃ is neutral and coordinated chlorido is −1, giving cobalt oxidation state +3. Its name is pentaamminechloridocobalt(III) chloride.

chapterName: Some Basic Principles of Organic Chemistry
en_questionText: Which carbocation is the most stable in the gas phase among the following?
en_explanation: Alkyl groups stabilize a carbocation through hyperconjugation and the +I effect. Therefore stability follows tertiary > secondary > primary > methyl.

en_questionText: Propene reacts with HBr in the absence of peroxides. The major product is:
en_explanation: Without peroxides, HBr adds to propene according to Markovnikov's rule through the more stable secondary carbocation, producing 2-bromopropane.

en_questionText: Which compound gives a positive Tollens' test under ordinary laboratory conditions?
en_explanation: Ethanal is an aldehyde and reduces Tollens' reagent to metallic silver. Propanone is a simple ketone, while ether and ethene do not give this test.

en_questionText: Which set of quantum numbers is not permissible for an electron in an atom?
en_explanation: For a given principal quantum number n, l may range only from 0 to n−1. Thus l = 2 is not allowed when n = 2; the other sets satisfy all quantum-number restrictions.

en_questionText: Given E°(Cu²⁺/Cu) = +0.34 V and E°(Zn²⁺/Zn) = −0.76 V, the standard emf of the Daniell cell Zn|Zn²⁺||Cu²⁺|Cu is:
en_explanation: Copper is the cathode and zinc is the anode. E°cell = E°cathode − E°anode = 0.34 − (−0.76) = 1.10 V.

en_questionText: A first-order reaction is 75% complete in 20 minutes. Its half-life is:
en_explanation: After 75% completion, 25% remains, equal to (1/2)². Therefore 20 minutes corresponds to two half-lives and t₁/₂ = 10 minutes.

en_questionText: The molecular shape of XeF₄ is:
en_explanation: XeF₄ has four bond pairs and two lone pairs arranged octahedrally. The lone pairs occupy opposite positions, leaving a square-planar molecular shape.

en_questionText: Which ion is colourless in aqueous solution because it has a completely filled d subshell?
en_explanation: Zn²⁺ has the 3d¹⁰ configuration and therefore no possible d-d transition. Cu²⁺, Ti³⁺ and Ni²⁺ have partially filled d subshells and are coloured.

en_questionText: The brown-ring test is used to detect which anion?
en_explanation: Nitrate is reduced by freshly prepared FeSO₄ to nitric oxide, which forms the brown nitrosyl complex [Fe(H₂O)₅NO]²⁺ at the acid-solution interface.

chapterName: Purification and Characterisation of Organic Compounds
en_questionText: Which method is most suitable for separating two miscible liquids whose boiling points differ by only a few kelvin?
en_explanation: A fractionating column provides repeated vaporisation-condensation cycles, allowing miscible liquids with close boiling points to be separated.

en_questionText: Which alkyl halide undergoes an SN1 reaction most readily in a polar protic solvent?
en_explanation: The rate-determining step in SN1 is carbocation formation. tert-Butyl chloride forms a stable tertiary carbocation, whereas primary, methyl and vinyl carbocations are much less favourable.

en_questionText: Aniline is less basic than cyclohexylamine mainly because:
en_optionA: The nitrogen lone pair in aniline is delocalised into the benzene ring
en_optionD: The nitrogen atom in aniline has no lone pair
en_explanation: Resonance delocalises the aniline nitrogen lone pair into the aromatic ring, making it less available for protonation than the localised lone pair of cyclohexylamine.

en_questionText: The linkage joining two α-amino acids in a polypeptide chain is called:
en_explanation: Condensation between the carboxyl group of one amino acid and the amino group of another forms the −CO−NH− peptide linkage.

en_questionText: The energy emitted when an electron in a hydrogen atom falls from n = 2 to n = 1 is:
en_explanation: For hydrogen, Eₙ = −13.6/n² eV. Thus emitted energy is E₂ − E₁ in magnitude: (−3.4) − (−13.6) = 10.2 eV.

en_questionText: A non-volatile solute has mole fraction 0.20 in an ideal binary solution. The relative lowering of the solvent vapour pressure is:
en_explanation: For a non-volatile solute in an ideal solution, (p°−p)/p° equals the solute mole fraction. Hence the relative lowering is 0.20.

en_questionText: A current of 1.0 A is passed through aqueous AgNO₃ for 9650 s. Taking Faraday constant F = 96500 C mol⁻¹, the mass of silver deposited is closest to:
en_explanation: Charge passed is 9650 C = 0.10 F, corresponding to 0.10 mol electrons. Since Ag⁺ + e⁻ → Ag, 0.10 mol Ag is deposited: mass = 0.10 × 107.9 ≈ 10.8 g.

en_questionText: According to molecular orbital theory, O₂ is paramagnetic because it contains:
en_optionA: Two unpaired electrons in antibonding π orbitals
en_optionB: One unpaired electron in a bonding σ orbital
en_optionD: Two unpaired electrons in bonding π orbitals
en_explanation: The two highest-energy electrons in O₂ occupy the degenerate π*2p orbitals singly, producing two unpaired electrons and paramagnetism.

chapterName: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties
en_questionText: Which element has the highest first ionisation enthalpy among B, C, N and O?
en_explanation: First ionisation enthalpy generally increases across the period. Nitrogen has the especially stable half-filled 2p³ configuration, so its value exceeds that of oxygen as well as carbon and boron.

en_questionText: The complex ion [Fe(CN)₆]⁴⁻ is diamagnetic because it contains:
en_optionA: Low-spin Fe²⁺ with no unpaired electrons
en_optionB: High-spin Fe²⁺ with four unpaired electrons
en_optionC: Low-spin Fe³⁺ with one unpaired electron
en_optionD: High-spin Fe³⁺ with five unpaired electrons
en_explanation: Iron is +2, giving d⁶. CN⁻ is a strong-field ligand, so the octahedral complex is low spin with configuration t₂g⁶ and no unpaired electrons.

chapterName: Some Basic Principles of Organic Chemistry
en_questionText: Phenol is more acidic than ethanol primarily because:
en_optionC: Phenol has a weaker O−H bond only because of higher molar mass
en_optionD: Ethanol forms more hydrogen bonds with water
en_explanation: Deprotonation of phenol gives phenoxide, whose negative charge is delocalised over the aromatic ring. The ethoxide ion lacks comparable resonance stabilisation.

en_questionText: Reductive ozonolysis of propene, CH₃CH=CH₂, produces:
en_explanation: Ozonolysis cleaves the C=C bond into carbonyl groups. The substituted carbon gives ethanal and the terminal CH₂ carbon gives methanal under reductive work-up.

en_questionText: Heating ethanol with concentrated H₂SO₄ at about 443 K mainly produces:
en_explanation: At about 443 K, concentrated sulphuric acid dehydrates ethanol intramolecularly to ethene. Lower temperatures favour intermolecular dehydration to ether.

en_questionText: Aniline is converted to benzenediazonium chloride by treatment with NaNO₂ and HCl at:
en_explanation: Diazotisation of aniline is carried out at 273–278 K because benzenediazonium chloride is stable only at low temperature and decomposes on warming.

en_questionText: For a reaction at 300 K, ΔH = −40 kJ mol⁻¹ and ΔS = −100 J mol⁻¹ K⁻¹. The value of ΔG and the spontaneity under these conditions are:
en_explanation: Convert ΔS to −0.100 kJ mol⁻¹ K⁻¹. Then ΔG = ΔH − TΔS = −40 − 300(−0.100) = −10 kJ mol⁻¹, so the reaction is spontaneous at 300 K.

en_questionText: For the gaseous equilibrium N₂O₄(g) ⇌ 2NO₂(g), the relation between Kp and Kc is:
en_explanation: Kp = Kc(RT)^Δn. Here Δn = 2 − 1 = 1, so Kp = Kc(RT).

en_questionText: For a reaction A + B → products, doubling [A] at constant [B] doubles the initial rate, while doubling both [A] and [B] increases the rate eightfold. The rate law is:
en_explanation: Doubling A alone doubles the rate, so the order in A is 1. With A doubled, the remaining factor needed for an eightfold increase is 4; hence doubling B gives 2ʸ = 4 and the order in B is 2.

en_questionText: BF₃ acts as a Lewis acid because:
en_optionA: Boron has an incomplete octet and can accept an electron pair
en_optionC: Boron has a lone pair available for donation
en_optionD: BF₃ releases OH⁻ ions in water
en_explanation: Boron in BF₃ has only six electrons in its valence shell and an empty orbital, so it can accept an electron pair and acts as a Lewis acid.

en_questionText: The gradual decrease in the radii of lanthanoid ions from La³⁺ to Lu³⁺ is mainly caused by:
en_optionA: Poor shielding of nuclear charge by 4f electrons
en_explanation: Across the lanthanoids, nuclear charge increases while 4f electrons shield poorly. The resulting rise in effective nuclear charge causes lanthanoid contraction.

en_questionText: The pair [Co(NH₃)₅(NO₂)]Cl₂ and [Co(NH₃)₅(ONO)]Cl₂ illustrates:
en_explanation: The ambidentate nitrite ligand coordinates through N in the nitro form and through O in the nitrito form, producing linkage isomers.

chapterName: Some Basic Principles of Organic Chemistry
en_questionText: Which compound can show geometrical (E/Z) isomerism?
en_explanation: Each double-bonded carbon in but-2-ene has two different substituents, allowing E/Z isomers. The other alkenes have identical substituents on at least one double-bonded carbon, or no double bond.

en_questionText: Nitration of toluene with concentrated HNO₃/H₂SO₄ gives mainly ortho- and para-nitrotoluene because the methyl group is:
en_explanation: The methyl group donates electron density through hyperconjugation and the +I effect, activating the ring and stabilising the ortho and para sigma complexes.

en_questionText: Chlorobenzene is much less reactive than chloroethane toward nucleophilic substitution mainly because:
en_optionA: The C−Cl bond in chlorobenzene has partial double-bond character due to resonance
en_optionC: The chlorine atom in chlorobenzene has no lone pairs
en_optionD: The carbon bonded to chlorine in chlorobenzene is sp³ hybridised
en_explanation: Resonance delocalisation of a chlorine lone pair into the aromatic ring gives the aryl C−Cl bond partial double-bond character, making it shorter and harder to break.

en_questionText: In double-stranded DNA, adenine pairs with thymine through:
en_explanation: Watson-Crick base pairing joins adenine and thymine by two hydrogen bonds; guanine and cytosine pair through three hydrogen bonds.

en_questionText: The freezing-point depression of a 0.10 mol kg⁻¹ aqueous glucose solution is closest to: (Kf for water = 1.86 K kg mol⁻¹)
en_explanation: Glucose is a non-electrolyte, so i = 1. Thus ΔTf = iKfm = 1 × 1.86 × 0.10 = 0.186 K.

en_questionText: A buffer contains equal molar concentrations of CH₃COOH and CH₃COONa at 25 °C. If pKa of CH₃COOH is 4.76, the pH of the buffer is:
en_explanation: For an acidic buffer, pH = pKa + log([salt]/[acid]). Equal concentrations make the logarithmic term zero, so pH = 4.76.

en_questionText: When chlorine reacts with cold, dilute NaOH, it forms NaCl and NaClO. In this reaction, chlorine undergoes:
en_optionA: Disproportionation from oxidation state 0 to −1 and +1
en_explanation: In Cl₂, chlorine has oxidation state 0. It is simultaneously reduced to −1 in Cl⁻ and oxidised to +1 in ClO⁻, so the reaction is disproportionation.

en_questionText: Which is the correct increasing order of acid strength of the oxoacids of chlorine?
en_explanation: For oxoacids with the same central atom, additional oxygen atoms increase the electron-withdrawing effect and stabilise the conjugate base. Hence acidity increases from HClO to HClO₄.

en_questionText: Propanoic acid is treated first with Br₂ in the presence of red phosphorus and then with water. The major organic product is:
en_explanation: The Hell–Volhard–Zelinsky reaction brominates the α-carbon of a carboxylic acid containing an α-hydrogen. Propanoic acid therefore gives CH₃CHBrCOOH, 2-bromopropanoic acid.

en_questionText: In bryophytes, the dominant, independent and photosynthetic plant body is the:
en_explanation: The bryophyte gametophyte is the dominant, free-living photosynthetic generation. The sporophyte remains attached to and nutritionally dependent on it.

chapterName: Structural Organisation in Animals and Plants
en_questionText: The vascular bundles in a typical monocot stem are described as closed because they:
en_optionA: Lack vascular cambium between xylem and phloem
en_explanation: A typical monocot stem has conjoint, collateral vascular bundles without cambium between xylem and phloem. Their lack of cambium makes them closed and normally prevents secondary growth.

en_questionText: Crossing over between homologous chromosomes normally occurs during which substage of prophase I of meiosis?
en_explanation: Synapsis begins in zygotene, while crossing over between non-sister chromatids of homologous chromosomes occurs during pachytene.

en_questionText: Cyclic electron flow around photosystem I directly results in the formation of:
en_optionA: ATP only, without NADPH or O₂ production
en_optionB: ATP and NADPH, with O₂ production
en_optionD: ATP and O₂, but no NADPH
en_explanation: In cyclic electron flow, electrons from photosystem I return to the electron transport chain. This generates a proton gradient for ATP synthesis but neither reduces NADP⁺ nor splits water, so NADPH and O₂ are not produced.

en_questionText: In a normal angiosperm with diploid sporophytic cells, double fertilisation produces a zygote and a primary endosperm nucleus with ploidies respectively:
en_explanation: One haploid male gamete fuses with the haploid egg to form a diploid zygote. The other fuses with two haploid polar nuclei to form the triploid primary endosperm nucleus.

en_questionText: Copper-releasing intrauterine devices primarily enhance contraception by:
en_optionA: Increasing phagocytosis of sperms and suppressing sperm motility and fertilising capacity
en_optionB: Preventing ovulation by continuously releasing high doses of estrogen
en_explanation: IUDs increase phagocytosis of sperms in the uterus, and released Cu²⁺ ions suppress sperm motility and fertilising capacity. They do not surgically block the oviducts or permanently destroy the endometrium.

en_questionText: The counter-current multiplier that establishes the medullary osmotic gradient in a mammalian kidney is formed mainly by the:
en_optionA: Oppositely directed flow in the descending and ascending limbs of the loop of Henle
en_optionB: Filtration across the glomerular capillaries and Bowman's capsule
en_optionC: Active secretion of H⁺ only in the proximal convoluted tubule
en_optionD: Movement of filtrate through the collecting duct alone
en_explanation: Opposite flow and different permeabilities in the two limbs of the loop of Henle multiply a small transverse gradient into the corticomedullary osmotic gradient. The vasa recta helps maintain this gradient by counter-current exchange.

en_questionText: The progressive weakening of immune responses in an untreated HIV infection is chiefly associated with depletion of:
en_explanation: HIV primarily infects and progressively depletes CD4⁺ helper T lymphocytes, impairing both cell-mediated and antibody-mediated immune responses.

en_questionText: The insecticidal protein produced by Bacillus thuringiensis is synthesised in the bacterium as an inactive protoxin that becomes active in the:
en_optionA: Alkaline gut of a susceptible insect larva
en_optionD: Bacterial cell by removal of its plasmid
en_explanation: Bt produces crystalline insecticidal proteins as inactive protoxins. The alkaline pH of a susceptible insect larva's gut solubilises and activates the toxin, which damages midgut epithelial cells.

en_questionText: Which option represents in situ conservation of biodiversity?
en_optionA: Protecting species within a national park
en_optionB: Maintaining seeds in a seed bank
en_optionD: Growing threatened plants only in a botanical garden
en_explanation: In situ conservation protects species in their natural habitats, as in national parks. Seed banks, cryopreservation and botanical gardens are ex situ approaches.

en_questionText: Which feature distinguishes Mycoplasma from most other prokaryotes?
en_explanation: Mycoplasma are very small prokaryotic organisms that lack a cell wall. They have a plasma membrane but no membrane-bound nucleus or chloroplasts.

chapterName: Structural Organisation in Animals and Plants
en_questionText: Which pair of plants characteristically shows axile placentation?
en_explanation: Tomato and lemon have axile placentation. Mustard and cucumber are parietal, sunflower and marigold are basal, while pea and bean are marginal.

en_questionText: A competitive inhibitor reduces enzyme activity primarily by:
en_optionA: Competing with the substrate for the enzyme's active site
en_optionC: Binding only to the enzyme-substrate complex at a distant site
en_optionD: Removing the product from the reaction mixture
en_explanation: A competitive inhibitor often resembles the substrate and reversibly occupies the active site, reducing substrate binding. Its effect can be diminished by increasing substrate concentration.

en_questionText: The net products formed during glycolysis from one molecule of glucose are:
en_explanation: Glycolysis in the cytosol converts one glucose into two pyruvate molecules, with a net gain of two ATP and two NADH. It does not directly release CO₂ or form acetyl-CoA.

en_questionText: Removal of the shoot apex commonly promotes the growth of lateral buds because it:
en_optionB: Stops cytokinin synthesis in the roots
en_optionC: Increases abscisic acid transport to lateral buds
en_optionD: Permanently prevents cell division in the stem
en_explanation: Auxin produced near the shoot apex helps maintain apical dominance and suppress lateral buds. Removing the apex lowers this auxin influence, allowing lateral buds to grow.

chapterName: Structural Organisation in Animals and Plants
en_questionText: In a cockroach, the Malpighian tubules arise near the junction of the:
en_explanation: Malpighian tubules are fine excretory tubules attached near the junction of the midgut and hindgut. They remove nitrogenous wastes from the haemolymph.

en_questionText: Which change shifts the oxyhaemoglobin dissociation curve to the right in actively respiring tissues?
en_optionA: An increase in partial pressure of CO₂
en_optionD: A decrease in partial pressure of CO₂
en_explanation: Higher CO₂ and H⁺ concentrations and higher temperature reduce haemoglobin's affinity for oxygen, shifting the curve to the right and facilitating oxygen release to active tissues.

en_questionText: The normal pacemaker of the human heart is the:
en_explanation: The sinoatrial node in the right atrium generates impulses at the highest intrinsic rate and normally initiates each heartbeat.

en_questionText: In the lac operon of Escherichia coli, the inducer permits transcription mainly by:
en_optionA: Binding to the repressor and preventing it from binding the operator
en_optionB: Binding to the operator and blocking RNA polymerase
en_optionD: Acting as a corepressor that activates the repressor
en_explanation: The inducer, effectively allolactose, binds the repressor and changes its conformation. The repressor can no longer bind the operator, allowing transcription of the structural genes.

en_questionText: In a population at Hardy-Weinberg equilibrium, the frequencies of two alleles are p = 0.7 and q = 0.3. The expected frequency of heterozygotes is:
en_explanation: At Hardy-Weinberg equilibrium, heterozygote frequency is 2pq. Therefore, 2 × 0.7 × 0.3 = 0.42.

en_questionText: In the standard taxonomic hierarchy, which category is immediately above genus?
en_explanation: The ascending taxonomic sequence includes species, genus, family, order and class. Therefore, family is immediately above genus.

en_questionText: Which statement correctly describes transport through the Golgi apparatus?
en_optionA: The cis face generally receives vesicles from the endoplasmic reticulum, while the trans face dispatches processed materials
en_optionB: The trans face receives newly synthesised proteins directly from ribosomes, while the cis face forms lysosomes
en_optionC: Both faces perform only ATP synthesis
en_optionD: The cis face contains DNA and the trans face contains ribosomes
en_explanation: The cis, or forming, face of the Golgi generally receives ER-derived vesicles. Modified and sorted products leave from the trans, or maturing, face.

en_questionText: In a typical C₄ plant, the first stable product of CO₂ fixation in mesophyll cells is:
en_explanation: PEP carboxylase fixes bicarbonate in mesophyll cells by adding it to phosphoenolpyruvate, producing the four-carbon compound oxaloacetate as the first stable product.

en_questionText: When fats are used predominantly as the respiratory substrate, the respiratory quotient is generally:
en_explanation: Respiratory quotient is CO₂ evolved divided by O₂ consumed. Oxidation of fats requires proportionally more oxygen than the carbon dioxide released, so the value is less than 1.

en_questionText: A short-day plant with a critical dark period of 10 hours is most likely to flower when it receives:
en_optionA: An uninterrupted dark period longer than 10 hours
en_optionB: An uninterrupted dark period shorter than 10 hours
en_optionC: A long dark period interrupted by a brief red-light exposure
en_optionD: Continuous light with no dark period
en_explanation: Short-day plants require a continuous dark period longer than a critical duration. A light interruption during the night can prevent flowering because the uninterrupted dark interval is decisive.

en_questionText: The methane-rich component of biogas is produced mainly by:
en_explanation: Methanogens such as Methanobacterium grow anaerobically in dung and sewage sludge and release methane, a major combustible component of biogas.

en_questionText: EcoRI cuts the sequence 5′-GAATTC-3′ between G and A on both strands in a staggered manner. The resulting DNA ends are:
en_explanation: Staggered cleavage by EcoRI at G↓AATTC produces complementary single-stranded 5′-AATT extensions, commonly called sticky or cohesive ends.

en_questionText: For a non-zero population following logistic growth, the growth rate dN/dt becomes zero when population size N reaches:
en_explanation: Logistic growth is described by dN/dt = rN(K − N)/K. For a non-zero population, the expression becomes zero at N = K, the environmental carrying capacity.

chapterName: Structural Organisation in Animals and Plants
en_questionText: The mature cells of cartilage that occupy spaces called lacunae are:
en_explanation: Mature cartilage cells are chondrocytes, and they lie within small cavities called lacunae in the cartilage matrix. Osteocytes occupy lacunae in bone.

en_questionText: In a normal human menstrual cycle, ovulation is triggered by a mid-cycle surge of:
en_explanation: A sharp mid-cycle rise in luteinising hormone causes rupture of the mature Graafian follicle and release of the secondary oocyte.

en_questionText: A person with blood group AB has the genotype IᴬIᴮ. This phenotype illustrates:
en_explanation: Iᴬ and Iᴮ are both expressed in an AB individual, producing both A and B antigens. Their simultaneous expression is codominance.

en_questionText: During transcription, RNA polymerase moves along the DNA template strand and synthesises RNA in which respective directions?
en_optionA: 3′→5′ along DNA and 5′→3′ for RNA synthesis
en_optionB: 5′→3′ along DNA and 3′→5′ for RNA synthesis
en_explanation: RNA polymerase reads the DNA template strand in the 3′→5′ direction and adds each ribonucleotide to the RNA 3′ end, so RNA grows 5′→3′.

en_questionText: During secondary sewage treatment, the biochemical oxygen demand of effluent decreases mainly because:
en_optionA: Aerobic microbial flocs consume much of the organic matter
en_optionB: Chlorine converts all organic matter directly into oxygen
en_optionC: Methanogens act aerobically in the aeration tank
en_optionD: Sedimentation alone converts organic matter into inorganic salts
en_explanation: In the aeration tank, aerobic microbial flocs oxidise a large fraction of the organic matter. The reduced organic load lowers the effluent's biochemical oxygen demand.

en_questionText: In a cloning vector, a selectable marker is used primarily to:
en_optionB: Join two DNA fragments by phosphodiester bonds
en_optionC: Cut DNA at a specific recognition sequence
en_optionD: Initiate DNA replication at the origin
en_explanation: A selectable marker, such as an antibiotic-resistance gene, permits cells carrying the vector to be identified or selected from cells that were not transformed.

en_questionText: An ecosystem has a gross primary productivity of 2000 kJ m⁻² yr⁻¹, while producers use 800 kJ m⁻² yr⁻¹ in respiration. Its net primary productivity is:
en_explanation: Net primary productivity equals gross primary productivity minus respiratory loss by producers: 2000 − 800 = 1200 kJ m⁻² yr⁻¹.

en_questionText: A taxonomic key is primarily based on:
en_optionA: Contrasting characters arranged in paired choices
en_optionB: Evolutionary age determined only from fossils
en_explanation: A taxonomic key identifies organisms through a sequence of paired, contrasting statements called couplets, with each choice directing the user toward another couplet or an identification.

en_questionText: Viroids differ from viruses because viroids consist of:
en_optionA: Small naked RNA molecules without a protein coat
en_optionB: DNA enclosed by a protein coat
en_optionC: RNA enclosed by a lipid envelope and capsid
en_optionD: Only protein molecules capable of replication
en_explanation: Viroids are infectious agents composed only of a small, circular RNA molecule and lack the protein coat present in viruses.

en_questionText: Which combination correctly describes pteridophytes?
en_optionA: Dominant vascular sporophyte and reproduction by spores
en_optionB: Dominant non-vascular gametophyte and seed formation
en_optionC: Vascular sporophyte with flowers and fruits
en_optionD: Non-vascular sporophyte independent of the gametophyte
en_explanation: Pteridophytes are seedless vascular plants with a dominant, independent sporophyte. They reproduce by spores rather than flowers, fruits or seeds.

chapterName: Structural Organisation in Animals and Plants
en_questionText: Pneumatophores in mangrove plants such as Avicennia mainly help in:
en_optionA: Gas exchange in waterlogged, oxygen-poor soil
en_optionD: Absorbing mineral salts from host tissue
en_explanation: Pneumatophores are negatively geotropic respiratory roots that project above waterlogged soil and bear openings for gaseous exchange.

chapterName: Structural Organisation in Animals and Plants
en_questionText: Heartwood in an old dicot stem is generally darker and non-conducting because its xylem elements:
en_optionA: Contain deposits such as resins and tannins and are often blocked by tyloses
en_optionB: Have newly formed companion cells conducting sugars
en_optionC: Retain active vascular cambium inside each vessel
en_optionD: Possess chloroplasts that absorb visible light
en_explanation: Heartwood consists of older secondary xylem infiltrated with substances such as resins, oils and tannins; vessels may be blocked by tyloses. It provides support but no longer conducts water efficiently.

en_questionText: Which polysaccharide is the principal storage carbohydrate in animals and is highly branched?
en_explanation: Glycogen is a highly branched polymer of glucose stored mainly in animal liver and muscle. Cellulose, chitin and pectin have chiefly structural roles.

en_questionText: Self-incompatibility promotes outcrossing in flowering plants by:
en_optionA: Preventing self-pollen from effecting fertilisation on a genetically related stigma
en_optionC: Ensuring that pollen is released only after fruit formation
en_optionD: Preventing meiosis in pollen mother cells
en_explanation: Self-incompatibility is a genetically controlled pollen-pistil interaction that rejects self or genetically related pollen, thereby preventing self-fertilisation and promoting outcrossing.

en_questionText: In the species-area relationship S = CAᶻ, a straight line is obtained by plotting:
en_explanation: Taking logarithms gives log S = log C + Z log A, which is a straight-line equation when log S is plotted against log A; Z is its slope.

chapterName: Structural Organisation in Animals and Plants
en_questionText: A typical skeletal muscle fibre is:
en_explanation: Skeletal muscle fibres are long, cylindrical, striated cells with many peripheral nuclei and are usually under voluntary control.

en_questionText: During anaphase I of meiosis in a diploid cell:
en_optionA: Homologous chromosomes separate while sister centromeres remain intact
en_optionB: Sister chromatids separate because centromeres divide
en_optionC: DNA replication occurs before homologues separate
en_explanation: Anaphase I is the reductional separation of homologous chromosomes. Their centromeres do not divide, so sister chromatids remain joined until anaphase II.

en_questionText: During early human pregnancy, human chorionic gonadotropin helps maintain the endometrium mainly by:
en_optionA: Maintaining the corpus luteum and its progesterone secretion
en_optionD: Stimulating milk ejection from mammary glands
en_explanation: hCG from trophoblastic tissue maintains the corpus luteum during early pregnancy. The corpus luteum continues secreting progesterone, which supports the endometrium.

en_questionText: During translation, the ribosome normally moves along mRNA and the polypeptide grows in which respective directions?
en_optionA: 5′→3′ along mRNA and from the amino terminus toward the carboxyl terminus
en_optionB: 3′→5′ along mRNA and from the carboxyl terminus toward the amino terminus
en_optionC: 5′→3′ along mRNA and from the carboxyl terminus toward the amino terminus
en_optionD: 3′→5′ along mRNA and from the amino terminus toward the carboxyl terminus
en_explanation: The ribosome reads codons on mRNA in the 5′→3′ direction. Each new amino acid is added to the carboxyl end, so the chain is synthesised from its amino terminus toward its carboxyl terminus.

en_questionText: A vaccinated person usually mounts a faster and stronger response on later exposure to the same antigen because vaccination generates:
en_optionB: A permanent increase in all neutrophils
en_optionD: Red blood cells carrying the antigen
en_explanation: Vaccination induces a primary adaptive immune response and forms antigen-specific memory B and T lymphocytes, which respond rapidly and strongly upon re-exposure.

en_questionText: The forelimbs of humans, whales and bats have the same basic skeletal plan but perform different functions. They are examples of:
en_optionD: Identical organs with no evolutionary significance
en_explanation: A shared basic structural plan inherited from a common ancestor makes these forelimbs homologous. Their modification for different functions illustrates divergent evolution.

en_questionText: RNA interference can silence a specific gene because introduced double-stranded RNA leads to:
en_optionA: Sequence-specific degradation or suppression of complementary mRNA
en_optionC: Permanent translation of all cellular mRNAs
en_optionD: Replacement of ribosomal RNA with DNA
en_explanation: Double-stranded RNA is processed into small interfering RNAs that guide a silencing complex to complementary mRNA, causing its degradation or blocking its expression.

en_questionText: A lichen is an association in which the photosynthetic partner mainly provides food, while the fungal partner mainly provides:
en_optionA: Shelter and absorption of water and minerals
en_optionD: Gametes for sexual reproduction of the alga
en_explanation: In a lichen, the alga or cyanobacterium supplies photosynthetic food, while the fungus provides protection, anchorage, water and mineral absorption.

en_questionText: Gymnosperms are described as having naked seeds because their ovules:
en_optionA: Are not enclosed within an ovary
en_optionB: Lack an integument at every stage
en_optionD: Are produced inside fruits without a pericarp
en_explanation: Gymnosperm ovules are exposed on reproductive structures rather than enclosed by an ovary. Consequently, their seeds are not enclosed within fruits.

en_questionText: According to the fluid mosaic model, a plasma membrane is best described as:
en_optionA: A fluid phospholipid bilayer with proteins embedded in or associated with it
en_optionB: A rigid protein sheet coated on both sides by lipids
en_optionC: A cellulose layer containing freely moving DNA
en_explanation: The fluid mosaic model describes a dynamic phospholipid bilayer in which integral and peripheral proteins form a mosaic and many components can move laterally.

en_questionText: A nucleotide differs from a nucleoside by the presence of:
en_explanation: A nucleoside contains a nitrogenous base joined to a pentose sugar. Addition of one or more phosphate groups produces a nucleotide.

en_questionText: Photorespiration begins when RuBisCO acts as an oxygenase and catalyses the reaction of O₂ with:
en_explanation: In photorespiration, RuBisCO oxygenates ribulose-1,5-bisphosphate, producing one molecule each of 3-phosphoglycerate and 2-phosphoglycolate.

en_questionText: In aerobic respiration, molecular oxygen functions at the end of the mitochondrial electron transport chain as the:
en_optionA: Final electron acceptor that is reduced to water
en_optionB: Initial electron donor that is oxidised to carbon dioxide
en_optionC: Carrier that transfers acetyl groups into the matrix
en_explanation: Oxygen accepts electrons and protons at the terminal step of the electron transport chain and is reduced to water. This permits continued electron flow and oxidative phosphorylation.

en_questionText: Application of gibberellin to a rosette plant can induce rapid internode elongation before flowering, a response called:
en_explanation: Gibberellins can cause rapid elongation of shortened internodes in rosette plants before flowering; this growth response is called bolting.

en_questionText: Unlike the carbon cycle, the phosphorus cycle has no significant atmospheric phase mainly because phosphorus:
en_optionA: Usually circulates through rocks, soil, water and organisms as non-volatile phosphates
en_optionC: Cannot dissolve in water under any condition
en_optionD: Is produced only by atmospheric nitrogen fixation
en_explanation: Phosphorus is mainly stored in rocks and sediments and moves as phosphate through soil, water and food webs. It lacks a substantial gaseous reservoir under ordinary biological conditions.

chapterName: Structural Organisation in Animals and Plants
en_questionText: The circulatory system of a cockroach is described as open because:
en_optionA: Haemolymph flows through body sinuses and is not confined to a closed network of vessels
en_optionB: Its heart opens directly to the exterior
en_optionC: Blood and tissue fluid are separated by capillary walls
en_optionD: Respiratory gases are transported only through veins
en_explanation: In an open circulatory system, haemolymph pumped by the dorsal vessel enters body sinuses and directly bathes the organs rather than remaining within a closed vascular network.

en_questionText: For each ATP hydrolysed by the sodium-potassium pump in a typical animal cell, the pump transports:
en_optionD: Equal numbers of Na⁺ and K⁺ in the same direction
en_explanation: The Na⁺/K⁺-ATPase is a primary active transporter that exports three Na⁺ ions and imports two K⁺ ions per ATP hydrolysed.

en_questionText: During human fertilisation, the acrosomal reaction helps a sperm primarily by:
en_optionA: Releasing enzymes that facilitate penetration of the egg coverings
en_optionB: Completing meiosis I in the sperm nucleus
en_optionC: Producing progesterone to maintain the endometrium
en_optionD: Forming the mitotic spindle of the zygote
en_explanation: The acrosome releases hydrolytic enzymes that help the sperm traverse the egg coverings, including the zona pellucida, before fusion with the oocyte membrane.

en_questionText: Two genes located very close together on the same chromosome generally show:
en_optionA: Linkage with a recombination frequency well below 50%
en_optionB: Independent assortment with exactly 50% recombination in every cross
en_explanation: Closely located genes are linked and are less likely to be separated by crossing over, so their recombination frequency is below 50% and often quite small.

en_questionText: During DNA replication, short Okazaki fragments are formed on the lagging strand and are joined by:
en_explanation: After replacement of RNA primers and filling of the resulting gaps, DNA ligase seals phosphodiester breaks between adjacent Okazaki fragments to make a continuous lagging strand.

en_questionText: The infective stage of Plasmodium that enters a human during the bite of an infected female Anopheles mosquito is the:
en_explanation: An infected female Anopheles injects sporozoites with its saliva. These travel to the liver and initiate the human phase of the malarial life cycle.

en_questionText: An expanding human population is represented by an age pyramid in which the:
en_optionA: Pre-reproductive group is larger than the reproductive group
en_optionB: Post-reproductive group is larger than both younger groups
en_optionC: Three age groups are approximately equal in size
en_explanation: A broad base with a relatively large pre-reproductive population indicates that many individuals will soon enter reproductive ages, producing positive population growth.

en_questionText: The sexual spores of ascomycete fungi are typically produced:
en_explanation: Ascomycetes form sexual ascospores endogenously within sac-like structures called asci. Basidiospores are produced externally on basidia.

en_questionText: Heterospory in Selaginella is considered an important step toward seed habit because it involves:
en_optionA: Production of distinct microspores and megaspores
en_optionD: A gametophyte that is always free-living and bisexual
en_explanation: Selaginella produces small microspores and large megaspores that form separate male and female gametophytes. Heterospory and retention of the megaspore foreshadow the seed habit.

chapterName: Structural Organisation in Animals and Plants
en_questionText: In an epigynous flower, the ovary is described as inferior because:
en_optionA: The other floral whorls appear to arise above the ovary
en_optionC: The sepals alone arise below the ovary
en_optionD: The ovules are exposed on a cone
en_explanation: In epigynous flowers, the thalamus surrounds and is fused with the ovary, so sepals, petals and stamens appear to arise above it. The ovary is therefore inferior.

chapterName: Structural Organisation in Animals and Plants
en_questionText: Kranz anatomy in a typical C₄ leaf is characterised by:
en_optionA: Prominent chloroplast-rich bundle-sheath cells arranged around vascular bundles
en_optionB: Absence of bundle-sheath cells around veins
en_optionC: Stomata restricted entirely to vascular tissue
en_optionD: A vascular cambium within every leaf bundle
en_explanation: C₄ leaves characteristically have large, chloroplast-rich bundle-sheath cells arranged in a wreath around vascular bundles, with mesophyll cells surrounding them.

en_questionText: An α-helix in a protein is stabilised mainly by hydrogen bonds between:
en_optionA: Peptide backbone C=O and N−H groups
en_optionC: R groups joined only by peptide bonds
en_explanation: The α-helix is a secondary protein structure stabilised by regular intrachain hydrogen bonds between backbone carbonyl oxygen and amide hydrogen groups.

en_questionText: Fixation of six CO₂ molecules through the Calvin cycle to yield one hexose requires:
en_explanation: Fixation of one CO₂ requires three ATP and two NADPH. Therefore, six CO₂ require 18 ATP and 12 NADPH to provide the net carbon equivalent of one hexose.

en_questionText: During controlled hybridisation, emasculation of a bisexual flower means:
en_optionA: Removing its anthers before they dehisce
en_optionC: Covering the flower without removing anthers
en_explanation: Emasculation removes anthers from the chosen female parent before pollen release, preventing self-pollination. The flower is then bagged until desired pollen is applied.

en_questionText: During water stress, abscisic acid helps limit water loss primarily by promoting:
en_optionD: Cell division in the vascular cambium
en_explanation: Abscisic acid accumulates during water stress and signals guard cells to close stomata, reducing transpiration and conserving water.

chapterName: Structural Organisation in Animals and Plants
en_questionText: Which feature is characteristic of cardiac muscle tissue?
en_optionA: Branched striated fibres connected by intercalated discs
en_optionB: Long unbranched fibres under voluntary control with no junctions
en_optionC: Spindle-shaped non-striated fibres with many peripheral nuclei
en_explanation: Cardiac muscle consists of involuntary, striated, branched cells joined by intercalated discs, which support coordinated contraction.

en_questionText: The volume of air inspired or expired during a normal quiet breath in a healthy adult is approximately:
en_explanation: Tidal volume is the air moved in or out during an ordinary quiet breath and is approximately 500 mL in a healthy adult.

en_questionText: If heart rate is 75 beats min⁻¹ and stroke volume is 70 mL beat⁻¹, cardiac output is:
en_explanation: Cardiac output equals heart rate multiplied by stroke volume: 75 × 70 = 5250 mL min⁻¹, or 5.25 L min⁻¹.

en_questionText: Antidiuretic hormone increases water conservation by increasing water permeability mainly in the:
en_optionC: Ascending limb of the loop of Henle only
en_explanation: ADH promotes insertion of aquaporins in cells of the late distal tubule and collecting duct, increasing water reabsorption and concentrating urine.

en_questionText: Immediately after meiosis I in spermatogenesis, each secondary spermatocyte has:
en_explanation: Meiosis I separates homologous chromosomes. Each secondary spermatocyte is haploid (n), but every chromosome still has two sister chromatids, giving 2C DNA.

en_questionText: Industrial melanism in peppered moths is best explained as a change in morph frequency caused by:
en_optionA: Differential survival and reproduction under natural selection
en_optionB: Individual moths darkening their wings in response to soot
en_optionC: Random transformation of all light moths into dark moths
en_optionD: Use and disuse of wing pigments during one lifetime
en_explanation: Environmental change altered camouflage and bird predation, so differently coloured inherited morphs had different survival and reproductive success. This is natural selection, not acquired change in individuals.

en_questionText: An immediate allergic response commonly involves allergen-specific IgE triggering mast cells to release:
en_explanation: Allergen cross-linking of IgE on sensitised mast cells causes degranulation and release of histamine and other mediators responsible for immediate allergy symptoms.

en_questionText: During a standard PCR cycle, Taq DNA polymerase extends primers most efficiently during the step performed near:
en_explanation: PCR commonly uses denaturation near 95 °C, primer annealing at a lower sequence-dependent temperature, and extension near 72 °C, the optimum for Taq polymerase.

en_questionText: During agarose gel electrophoresis, DNA fragments move toward the anode primarily because DNA:
en_optionC: Is electrically neutral but attracted by agarose
en_optionD: Contains ATP that moves toward positive electrodes
en_explanation: The phosphate backbone gives DNA a net negative charge, so DNA migrates toward the positive electrode. Smaller fragments generally move faster through the gel matrix.

en_questionText: An orchid growing as an epiphyte on a mango branch exemplifies commensalism because:
en_optionA: The orchid gains support while the mango is neither helped nor harmed
en_optionC: The orchid kills and consumes mango tissue
en_optionD: The mango benefits while the orchid is harmed
en_explanation: The epiphytic orchid obtains physical support and better access to light, while the mango tree is generally unaffected, which defines commensalism.

en_questionText: In primary succession on bare rock, the usual pioneer community consists mainly of:
en_explanation: Lichens can colonise bare rock, weather its surface and contribute organic matter, helping form soil for later communities in primary succession.

en_questionText: Which litter would generally decompose most slowly under otherwise similar conditions?
en_optionA: Litter rich in lignin and chitin
en_optionB: Litter rich in soluble sugars and nitrogen
en_optionC: Soft leaf litter with little lignin
en_optionD: Finely fragmented litter with abundant moisture
en_explanation: Lignin and chitin are resistant to microbial breakdown, so litter rich in them decomposes slowly. Soluble nutrients, fragmentation and adequate moisture generally accelerate decomposition.

en_questionText: The most important current cause of biodiversity loss worldwide is:
en_explanation: Destruction and fragmentation of natural habitats eliminate populations and isolate survivors, making habitat loss the leading component of contemporary biodiversity decline.

en_questionText: In normal human development, implantation in the uterine endometrium begins when the embryo is at the:
en_explanation: After cleavage and formation of a morula, a blastocyst develops. Its trophoblast attaches to and invades the uterine endometrium during implantation.

en_questionText: For an X-linked recessive disorder, an affected father (XʰY) and a homozygous unaffected mother (XᴴXᴴ) will have:
en_optionA: All daughters as carriers and all sons unaffected
en_optionB: All daughters affected and all sons unaffected
en_optionC: Half the sons affected and all daughters unaffected non-carriers
en_explanation: Every daughter receives Xʰ from the father and Xᴴ from the mother, so all are carriers. Every son receives Y from the father and Xᴴ from the mother, so all are unaffected.

en_questionText: Down syndrome most commonly results from:
en_optionC: An extra Y chromosome in every female
en_explanation: Down syndrome is most commonly caused by meiotic nondisjunction producing an extra copy of chromosome 21, giving trisomy 21.

en_questionText: The genetic code is described as degenerate because:
en_optionA: More than one codon can specify the same amino acid
en_optionB: One codon normally specifies several amino acids simultaneously
en_optionC: Every codon is a stop codon
en_optionD: Codons are read without a fixed direction
en_explanation: Most amino acids are specified by more than one codon. This redundancy is called degeneracy; an individual codon remains unambiguous for a particular amino acid or stop signal.

en_questionText: Two bodies of unequal masses attract each other gravitationally. The force on the heavier body is:
en_optionA: Equal in magnitude to the force on the lighter body
en_optionB: Greater because the body is heavier
en_optionC: Smaller because the body is heavier
en_optionD: Zero if the heavier body is at rest
en_explanation: The gravitational interaction obeys Newton's third law: each body experiences equal-magnitude, opposite-direction force.

en_questionText: At an altitude equal to Earth's radius above its surface, the acceleration due to gravity is approximately:
en_explanation: The distance from Earth's centre is 2R, so g' = g(R/2R)² = g/4.

en_questionText: According to Kepler's second law, the line joining a planet to the Sun sweeps out:
en_optionA: Equal areas in equal intervals of time
en_optionB: Equal angles in equal intervals of time
en_optionC: Equal distances in equal intervals of time
en_optionD: Areas proportional to the planet's speed
en_explanation: Kepler's area law states that the radius vector sweeps equal areas in equal times.

en_questionText: A planet has surface gravitational acceleration 10 m s⁻² and radius 6.4 × 10⁶ m. Its escape speed is closest to:

A satellite moving in a stable circular orbit with speed vᴄ is given a small tangential speed increase to v'. Immediately afterward, at the same radius, the gravitational force available compared with the centripetal force required to maintain circular motion at speed v' is:
en_explanation: Initially, gravity supplies mvᴄ²/r. Immediately after the increase, gravity is unchanged, while circular motion at v' > vᴄ would require mv'²/r, which is larger. Thus gravity is insufficient to maintain circular motion at that speed and radius.
